method: Fresh verifier sub-agent researched the story independently (found Anthropic's own 11 Aug and 14 Aug posts, plus TechCrunch and The Register coverage), then a fresh adversarial falsifier sub-agent (separate context) tried to break each claim and confirmed the mechanism description, the 'not yet shipped' status of the detection API, and the absence of any prior noiseless-news coverage. Both agents flagged a candidate claim -- Business Insider's report of users canceling Claude subscriptions over the watermark -- as anecdote-only (four named subscribers plus unverified social-media posts) with Anthropic itself denying any measurable cancellation uptick to BI; that claim was dropped from the published article rather than published as a hedged business fact, since no second independent source with real data was found.
origin_items: Surfaced from this cycle's fresh ingest (data/raw/2026-08-15/the-decoder.json, techcrunch-ai.json, gnews-ai-litigation.json, gnews-ai-regulation-and-policy.json, techmeme.json) covering Anthropic's 14 August technical follow-up post on Claude's text watermark.

claims.text: On 11 August 2026, Anthropic announced it would begin embedding a statistical watermark in text generated by Claude models, citing compliance with the EU AI Act's transparency Code of Practice
claims.reasoning: Confirmed by TechCrunch (11 Aug 2026) and The Register (11 Aug 2026), both tying the move explicitly to the EU AI Act Transparency Code (effective 2 Aug 2026); referenced by Anthropic's own 14 Aug follow-up post.

claims.text: On 14 August 2026, Anthropic published technical detail on the mechanism: for interchangeable, low-stakes word choices, it biases token selection using a secret key plus preceding context -- an approach it says is in the same family as Google DeepMind's SynthID-Text
claims.reasoning: Directly fetched from Anthropic's own post (dated 14 Aug 2026), which describes changing 'the source of randomness used when making some of those choices' using 'the key and a few words that come before,' and explicitly cites SynthID-Text (Google DeepMind, Nature 2024) as the same family of technique. Cross-confirmed by TechCrunch and The Register (15 Aug 2026), no outlet disputes the description.

claims.text: Anthropic says the watermark is not applied to code and is faint in text tightly constrained by facts; it survives light editing but is lost under heavy rewriting, paraphrasing, or translation
claims.reasoning: Stated directly in Anthropic's post; matches TechCrunch and Register summaries verbatim on the code/fact-constrained-text limitation and the light-edit-vs-rewrite distinction.

claims.text: Anthropic says it will soon offer a watermark detection API for third parties but has not yet released it and is still finalizing the implementation
claims.reasoning: Anthropic's exact wording is future tense ('We will soon be offering a watermark detection API... still in the process of working out the details'). Falsifier searched independently and found no credible report of the API having shipped as of 15-16 Aug 2026; one low-quality outlet (techtimes.com) ran an internally-contradictory piece implying the API was live while also stating Anthropic hadn't released the detector -- excluded as unreliable.

claims.text: Anthropic states the watermark does not prove authorship: it can only indicate Claude was likely involved, cannot distinguish text Claude wrote from text it heavily edited, and cannot identify output from other companies' AI systems
claims.reasoning: Verbatim from Anthropic's post: the watermark 'can only determine that Claude was likely involved... cannot distinguish "Claude wrote this" from "Claude heavily edited this."'
